sentences.text: [serious] Pay them a cow, or they burn your farm.
Four hundred years ago, that was normal on the England-Scotland border.
Raiding families called reivers stole every cow they could drive home.
Legend says when one family ran out of food, the wife served a plate holding nothing but spurs.
So farmers started paying the raiders to stay away.
[curious] And the name for it? You still say it today.
Mail meant rent. Paid in silver, it was white mail.
Then England made paying blackmail a crime you could hang for.
The robbed farmers faced the rope too.
Pay and hang, or refuse and burn: which would you pick?
